record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For completely positive maps T from trace-class operators to Schatten p-class operators, decide whether maximal output p-norm multiplicativity holds globally, especially for 1 <= p <= 2: is the maximal output p-norm of T1 tensor T2 always equal to the product of the maximal output p-norms of T1 and T2? This related conjecture would imply additivity of minimal output entropy as p decreases to 1 and is tied to the additivity of the Holevo quantity and entanglement of formation.

evidence.quote:
If the conjecture is valid, then the additivity of χ tentatively relies upon yet another hypothetical property of multiplicativity of norms of the completely positive mappings
T : ℓ1(H) → ℓp(H); p ≥ 1
By letting p ↓ 1 this implies additivity of the minimal output entropy
The standing conjecture is that multiplicativity holds globally at least for 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, but even the case p = 2 is difficult

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable complex Hilbert space. For p ≥ 1, let S_p(H) denote the Schatten p-class of compact operators on H with norm ‖A‖_p = (Tr|A|^p)^{1/p}, and let S_1(H) be the trace class. A linear map T : S_1(H) → S_p(H) is called completely positive if for every n ≥ 1 the amplification T ⊗ id_{M_n} sends positive elements to positive elements. For such a map T, define its maximal output p-norm by

  ν_p(T) := sup { ‖T(ρ)‖_p : ρ ∈ S_1(H), ρ ≥ 0, Tr ρ = 1 }.

Given two completely positive maps T_1 : S_1(H_1) → S_p(K_1) and T_2 : S_1(H_2) → S_p(K_2), their tensor product T_1 ⊗ T_2 : S_1(H_1 ⊗ H_2) → S_p(K_1 ⊗ K_2) is the unique completely positive map satisfying (T_1 ⊗ T_2)(A ⊗ B) = T_1(A) ⊗ T_2(B).

Question: Does the multiplicativity identity

  ν_p(T_1 ⊗ T_2) = ν_p(T_1) · ν_p(T_2)

hold for all such completely positive maps T_1, T_2 and all p with 1 ≤ p ≤ 2? In particular, does it hold in the case p = 2?
artifact.status_search_result: The global multiplicativity conjecture for maximal output p-norms has been disproved. Hayden and Winter (Commun. Math. Phys., 2008; arXiv:0807.4753) constructed counterexamples for all p > 1, including arbitrarily close to 1, ruling out multiplicativity in the range 1 < p ≤ 2. The case p = 1 is trivial. Consequently, the strong multiplicativity property as stated does not hold globally; additivity of minimum output (von Neumann) entropy was separately disproved by Hastings (2009).

status_evidence.title: Counterexamples to the Maximal p-Norm Multiplicativity Conjecture for all p > 1
status_evidence.snippet: For all p > 1, there exist quantum channels whose maximal output p-norm is not multiplicative under tensor product.
status_evidence.claim: Multiplicativity of the maximal output p-norm fails for every p > 1, including p in (1,2].

status_evidence.title: The maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture is false
status_evidence.claim: The multiplicativity conjecture fails for 1 < p < 2.

status_evidence.title: The maximum output p-norm of quantum channels is not multiplicative for any p>2
status_evidence.snippet: Winter establishes non-multiplicativity for all p > 2.
status_evidence.claim: Non-multiplicativity holds for p > 2 as well.
